paper.title: Parallel random numbers: as easy as 1, 2, 3 (Threefry generators)
paper.venue: Proceedings of SC '11 (International Conference for High Performance Computing, Networking, Storage and Analysis)

program.how: written for ounce-core from the paper's Threefry construction (counter + key, add/rotate/xor rounds on word pairs, key injection every 4 rounds, Threefish key-schedule parity constant); the rotation constants (which come from the Threefish reference sources) and the key-schedule parity were read as numbers from the authors' header; no third-party code copied
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: Threefry 2x32, 4x32, 2x64 and 4x64 at 13, 20 and 32 (2-word) or 72 (4-word) rounds, each for the three counter/key pairs the authors list (all zeros, all ones, digits of pi): all 36 known-answer vectors match

expected_values_source.what: the 36 threefry lines of the Random123 authors' tests/kat_vectors file
expected_values_source.note: the vectors are data, copied as numbers; the authors' header was read for the rotation constants and to confirm the key-injection layout and was not copied. The sibling Philox generator of the same paper is covered by the separate philox/ check (this folder does not repeat it). Note: in the kat_vectors lines for threefry4x64 at 20 and 72 rounds with the digits-of-pi counter, the fourth key word equals the third (be5466cf34e90c6c twice) where the 13-round line has c0ac29b7c97c50dd; the program uses the key exactly as the file lists it and the listed outputs match, so this looks like a harmless oddity in the test file, not an implementation difference

negative_control: built with -DTF_INJECT=5 (a key injection after every 5 rounds instead of 4), 0 of 36 vectors match and the program exits 1 (checked on ounce-core Tier-3 and natively)
not_checked: the paper's statistical claims (BigCrush results for Threefry and Philox), its crush-resistance and security discussion, and the Philox generators
Threefry with a number of rounds other than the ones listed
the paper's counter-based API, streams and its performance tables
speed figures (emulator run time says nothing about the authors' hardware)
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, produces exactly the 36 published Threefry known-answer vectors. It does not show the statistical claims hold.
